corrections.reason: audit 2026-09-16: the 4,320 is a DOLLAR figure, not a headcount. The document is a Q2 2026 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1 to an 8-K). Its only occurrence of 4,320 is a line in the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation table headed '(in thousands, except percentages)': 'Integration and restructuring costs (2) 2,047 1,336 4,320 3,377', i.e. $4.32 million of integration and restructuring cost for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Footnote (2), which is the row's stored excerpt, reads in full 'Includes acquisition integration and restructuring costs, including plant consolidation and reconfiguration, reductions in force, and executive severance expense.' The release states no number of employees, positions or reductions anywhere; every match for 'employees', 'positions', 'workforce' or 'reduction in force' in the text was read and none carries a count. A reduction in force did occur at some size, but the source supports NO count, which is the trash case, not a recount.
corrections.evidence: The earnings release was fetched and read in full for this audit (283 KB HTML, 20,776 characters of text); the table line and footnote are quoted above verbatim.
corrections.command: WP_SITE_URL=... WP_API_KEY=... python3 railway/apply_correction.py --ids 177216 --action trash --verify-company 'Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc.' --reason '<the reason field above>' --apply

corrections.reason: audit 2026-09-16: a third-party economic-impact PROJECTION, not an employer announcement, and not the employer's own jobs. The article's first sentence: 'The merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. could cost about 4,500 film and TV jobs over three years, according to a new report issued by Los Angeles County.' The report is by a consultancy commissioned by a county supervisor; the 4,500 are regional film and TV production jobs across the L.A. economy over three years, not positions at the registrant, and the article goes on to size a 'ripple effect' at 10,360. The employer did not announce this and disputes its framing: 'In response, Paramount issued a statement arguing that the report proves its point about the dire state of Hollywood's production economy.' The event itself has not happened: 'The Paramount-Warner Bros. merger is on hold at least through March 2027, when a trial is scheduled on the antitrust lawsuit brought by 12 state attorneys general.' Under adjudication rule 3 the count is unsupported for any employer event; the row is also wrongly flagged announced=1 and wrongly attributes the number to a combined company that does not exist. Reclassifying to announced=0 would still leave a 4,500 row for a layoff nobody announced and no employer will conduct, so the action is trash.
corrections.evidence: The article was fetched and read in full for this audit; the four sentences above are quoted verbatim.
corrections.command: WP_SITE_URL=... WP_API_KEY=... python3 railway/apply_correction.py --ids 178667 --action trash --verify-company 'Paramount-Warner Bros.' --reason '<the reason field above>' --apply

corrections.reason: audit 2026-09-16: the same county projection as row 178667, at its earlier (June) size, read out of a background paragraph. The article's sentence: 'In Los Angeles County alone, the merger could result in a loss of nearly 2,500 jobs, according to an analysis by the Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity, published in June.' The next sentence is speculative too: 'As many as 6,000 employees around the world could also see their positions cut.' The article is about the CEO threatening to move operations out of California over the stalled merger; the merger is paused ('On July 24, Paramount Skydance agreed to pause the merger until a ruling in the states' case is ultimately made or until June 1, 2027'). The only employer-attributed headcount in the piece is retrospective and a different event: 'when the Paramount and Skydance merger was completed in 2025, the company laid off roughly 2,000 people.' No employer announced a 2,500-job cut on or around 2026-08-11, so the count is unsupported (adjudication rule 3) and announced=1 is wrong. The row also sits in a different month-bucket from 178667 for the same projection, so it double counts a number that should not be present once. Trash.
corrections.evidence: The article was fetched and read in full for this audit; the sentences above are quoted verbatim. This row is stored under country 'Multiple countries' and does not enter the US August figures on either basis; it is included here because the first reader flagged it as a US row and the reading is the same.
